title: Mass tenant re-pin warroom runbook
content:
Purpose
------
Ad-hoc operational runbook for coordinating a mass tenant region re-pin when an entire region becomes unavailable or legally blocked and customers must be reassigned to alternate anchors quickly and audibly. This doc is focused on execution (warroom), safe rollforward, communications, and fast rollback. It is intentionally terse and action-oriented.

Scope
-----
- Applies to multi-tenant Private deployments and Dedicated customers where region pins are active.
- Not for standard single-tenant migrations (see tenant-pin-migration-execution-template).
- Triggered when more than 50 tenants in a single region require re-pinning within a 24h window OR when region-level outage prevents servicing pinned traffic.

Before the warroom (pre-checks)
-------------------------------
- Confirm the trigger: run query 'region_pin_event_counts(region, last_24h)' and validate count > threshold.
- Confirm legal/contract requirement: check linked_contraacts list and contact legal lead.
- Allocate warroom Slack channel: #warroom-repin-<region>-<date>.
- Pager duty: notify eng-oncall + product-ops + customer-success.
- Snapshot current pin state: run 'pin-state-export --region <R> --output /tmp/pin-snapshot-<ts>.ndjson' and upload to S3 bucket 'residency-backups'.

Warroom roles (minimal)
----------------------
- Warroom lead (WL): coordinates steps, gatekeeper for communications (example: WL = Maya).
- Operator lead (OL): runs re-pin orchestration, monitors pipelines (example: OL = Owen).
- Telemetry lead (TL): runs queries, sanity checks, metrics (example: TL = Isha).
- Customer liaison (CL): drafts outbound messages, coordinates CS teams (example: CL = Luca).
- Legal/Compliance: consulted as necessary.
- SRE: ensures system-level capacity for surge.

Immediate warroom checklist (first 30 minutes)
---------------------------------------------
1) Create warroom channel and pinned resources (RFC, snapshots, deploy manifests).
2) Share authoritative list of impacted tenants (run 'list-impacted-tenants --region <R> --since 24h > /tmp/impacted.txt').
3) Confirm fallback anchors available in target regions and capacity reservations. If capacity is low, throttle re-pin batch sizes.
4) Put a soft pause on automated pin-change-scheduler to prevent overlap. (API: PATCH /ops/config/scheduler {enabled:false})
5) Ensure KMS key locality compatibility: run 'kms-compat-check --tenants /tmp/impacted.txt' and escalate if any tenant requires key relocation.
6) Snapshot quotas/billing flags for impacted tenants for reconciliation.

Phased execution plan (safe fast path)
-------------------------------------
Phase A - Dry-run (small sample, ~5 tenants)
- Goal: validate orchestration path, telemetry, and rollback.
- Steps: pick 5 low-risk tenants (CS-approved), run re-pin run with --dry-run=false but in low rate, monitor for errors for 15 minutes.
- Success criteria: 200 OK from pin API, KV-caches primed in target region, no failed webhook deliveries, 95th percentile latency within 2x baseline.

Phase B - Incremental batches (50-200 tenants per batch depending on capacity)
- Use exponential backoff between batches and checkpoint after each.
- Typical batch commands: 're-pin-batch --input /tmp/impacted.txt --batch-size 100 --target-region <R2> --mode orchestrated --notify /tmp/batch-<n>.log'
- For each batch: run post-batch health checks and data locality verification.

Phase C - Catch-up and cleanup
- Handle remaining tenants with special needs (KMS, legal holds).
- Run audit-record generation 'pin-change-evidence --batch /tmp/batch-<n>.log --format ndjson' and upload.
- Re-enable scheduler after final validation.

Operator commands and shortcuts
------------------------------
- pin-export: pin-export --region R --since 2026-02-01 --out=s3://residency-backups/region-R-snapshot.ndjson\- bulk-repin: bulk-repin --file /tmp/batch-input.ndjson --target R2 --concurrency 8 --dry-run=false\- throttle: opsctl traffic-quota set --region R2 --limit 70%\- rollback-batch: bulk-repin --rollback --file /tmp/batch-<n>.ndjson\- evidence: pin-change-evidence --batch /tmp/batch-<n>.log --upload s3://residency-evidence/<region>/<ts>.json

Telemetry checks (queries to run after every batch)
--------------------------------------------------
- Active-traffic-by-tenant: 'metrics.query("tenant.requests", {region: "R2", window: "5m"})'
- Pin-failure-rate: 'pin.metrics.failures.count(region="R2", since="15m")'
- KV-cache-warmth: 'cache.hit_rate(region="R2", model_family="*", window=10m)'
- End-to-end latency: p95 and p99 for affected tenants vs baseline.
- Error-sampling: flip on debug sampling for 1% of traffic for 20 minutes to collect traces.

Safety and rollback conditions (abort and rollback triggers)
---------------------------------------------------------
- Abort and rollback if any of the following within 30 minutes of batch:
  - pin-failure-rate > 2% AND absolute failed tenants > 10 OR
  - p95 latency > 3x baseline AND customer SLA at risk OR
  - any legal hold tenant is moved (immediate rollback for those tenants)
Rollback steps (fast)
1) Pause new batches.
2) Run 'rollback-batch --file /tmp/recent-batch.ndjson --target-region original --concurrency 4'.
3) Rehydrate caches in original region if needed: 'cache.prefill --source original --tenants /tmp/rollback-list'.
4) Notify customers and open a postmortem.

Customer and internal comms templates (short)
--------------------------------------------
Internal status update (to execs):
- Subject: [Warroom] Mass region re-pin for <region> — progress update
- Body: 3-line status, batches completed X/Y, top risk, ETA for full completion, major actions.

Customer-facing (CS short script):
- "We detected region-level impact and are proactively reassigning your tenant to an alternative region to maintain service. Expected impact: brief config update (transparent to your app). We will notify when complete and provide evidence package on request."

Post-incident deliverables
-------------------------
- Upload final pin-state snapshot to evidence bucket.
- Complete incident timeline in Jira (JIRA-PIN-7890).
- Postmortem doc with root cause, what worked, and itemized action plan (owner + due date).
- Billing reconciliation: reconcile billed vs reserved capacity for target region.

Operational concerns & edge cases
--------------------------------
- KMS-bound tenants: these must be identified and handled with Legal + Security signoff; in many cases we must broker a legal path before moving keys.
- Subprocessor clauses: double-check contract clauses for cross-border subprocessor restrictions before wholesale moves.
- Long-lived session affinity: customers using sticky session cookies may observe session breaks — plan for session re-establishment guidance.
- Auditability: preserve evidence artifacts in immutable storage with timestamps.

Runbook TL;DR (one-pager)
-------------------------
1) Create warroom, snapshot pins, list impacted tenants.
2) Run 1 dry-run sample -> validate telemetry.
3) Incremental batches with telemetry gates.
4) If failure triggers, pause and rollback last batch.
5) Prepare evidence and comms, then postmortem.

Notes-to-self and TODOs
----------------------
- Add automation to precompute per-tenant KMS compatibility and surface early during onboarding.
- Automate batch-size suggestion based on available GPU pools (opsctl suggestion engine).
- Add canned customer evidence package generator to reduce manual work.

Slack and contact references
--------------------------
- Warroom channel pattern: #warroom-repin-<region>-<YYYYMMDD>
- Oncall escalation: @eng-oncall, @sre-oncall, legal@redwood-inference.com
- External CS template doc: confluence/redwood/residency/customer-comm-templates (CONFLUENCE-1234)

End of doc. Keep this file lean — expand small helper scripts into the orchestration repo.
